title: Pointed base change and standard shrinking of devissage data
statement: Use the pointed affine one-step data, chains, and standard shrinkings of [def-trf-pointed-scheme-devissage-data]. The following operations preserve those data. (1) Given an affine pointed map $(B',b')\to(B,b)$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(b)\to\kappa(b')$, base change of a one-step datum or chain, with the unique points above all old marked points in the fibre over $b'$, is again such a datum or chain. All smooth relative dimensions are unchanged; for a chain the maps $\alpha_j$ are pulled back using the canonical finite-pushforward base-change isomorphisms. Their cokernels are the pullbacks of the old cokernels. (2) A one-step datum can be standardly shrunk after any prescribed principal open restriction of the base containing $b$. For any principal open $W\subset Y$ containing $y$, it has a standard shrinking with new base a principal open $B'\subset B$ containing $b$ and new target $Y'=W\times_BB'$. For any open $U\subset X$ containing $x$, it has a standard shrinking with initial scheme contained in $U$. If a map $\alpha:\mathcal O_Y^{\oplus r}\to\pi_*\mathcal G$ has an isomorphism on the generic residue-field vector space of $Y_b$, its restriction has that property and its cokernel restricts to the old cokernel. (3) A chain can be standardly shrunk after any prescribed principal open restriction of the base, inside any prescribed open neighbourhood of its initial marked point, or with its last target equal to $W\times_BB'$ for a prescribed principal open neighbourhood $W$ of its last marked point, after shrinking the base to $B'$. All inclusions in standard shrinkings preserve marked residue fields. The statements include chains of length zero, with the last-target request made only for positive length.

source.place: Tags 05HA (lemma-shrink), 05HK (lemma-base-change-complete-at-x), 05HM (lemma-shrink-complete), with 05H7 and 05HJ for the one-step and complete base-change comparisons; the proofs preserve the auxiliary data without support-dimension equalities.

proof.text: First base-change a single datum. Write $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $B'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$. The fibre-product formula makes all four new schemes affine. The pulled-back $X'\to B'$ is locally of finite type; $i'$ is a closed immersion of finite presentation, $\pi'$ is finite, and $Y'\to B'$ is smooth of the same relative dimension $d$, by the cited permanence statements. For a point $c'\in B'$ above $c\in B$, the fibre of $Y'$ is $Y_c\times_{\kappa(c)}\kappa(c')$: on rings this is $(T\otimes_A A')\otimes_{A'}\kappa(c')=T\otimes_A\kappa(c')$. After a further field extension it is still a field extension of $Y_c$, so is irreducible by the definition of geometrically irreducible. Thus every new fibre has the required geometric irreducibility. The fibre dimensions follow. Since $Y\to B$ is locally of finite presentation [lem-pc-smooth-flat], each old fibre $Y_c$ is locally of finite type over $\kappa(c)$ and irreducible of dimension $d$, so every point of $Y_c$ has local dimension $d$ [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension]; thus $Y\to B$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and so is $Y'\to B'$. Each new fibre is the spectrum of the finitely generated $\kappa(c')$-algebra $T\otimes_A\kappa(c')$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; it is irreducible, and all its local dimensions are $d$, so it has dimension $d$ [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components].

source.place: 05H7, lemma-base-change-one-step, geometric part; support-dimension comparison omitted for the auxiliary definition

proof.text: The pullbacks of $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent. On affine opens pullback is $M\mapsto M\otimes_R R'$; if $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ generate $M$, their tensors $m_i\otimes1$ generate the pullback. The affine finite-type criterion therefore preserves finite type. Apply affine pushforward base change to $i$: pulling back $i_*\mathcal G\cong\mathcal F$ gives $i'_*\mathcal G'\cong\mathcal F'$. Apply it also to $\pi$ to identify the new pushforward with the pullback of $\pi_*\mathcal G$. These maps are affine since their sources and targets are affine; on rings the comparison is $R'\otimes_R M\cong(R'\otimes_R D)\otimes_D M$, $a'\otimes m\mapsto(a'\otimes1)\otimes m$, with inverse $(a'\otimes d)\otimes m\mapsto a'\otimes dm$.

At the chosen point the preceding fibre formula becomes $T\otimes_A\kappa(b')\cong T\otimes_A\kappa(b)$, because the specified map $\kappa(b)\to\kappa(b')$ is an isomorphism. It identifies the entire marked fibres, their points, residue fields, and the maps $i_b,\pi_b$. In particular there are unique new $x',z',y'$ over the old marked points and $b'$, $i'(z')=x'$, $\pi'(z')=y'$, and the fibre over $y'$ is a singleton. The extension $\kappa(y')/\kappa(b')$ is the old purely transcendental extension under these identifications. Together with steps 1--2 this verifies every condition of the pointed one-step definition, without any assumption on support dimensions.

For a chain pull back each $\alpha_j$, using the pushforward comparison of step 2. On an affine target with coefficient module $N_j$, the exact sequence $R_j^{r_j}\xrightarrow{\alpha_j}N_j\to Q_j\to0$ becomes $R_j'^{r_j}\to N_j\otimes_{R_j}R_j'\to Q_j\otimes_{R_j}R_j'\to0$ by right exactness of tensor. The quasi-coherent cokernel is computed by this quotient on affine opens, so the new cokernel is precisely the old cokernel pulled back. At the generic point $\xi'_j$ the pullback-stalk formula, followed by tensoring with $\kappa(\xi'_j)$, identifies the new residue-field map with the old one extended from $\kappa(\xi_j)$ to $\kappa(\xi'_j)$. Here $\xi'_j$ corresponds to $\xi_j$ under step 3. Tensoring an isomorphism preserves its inverse. Hence the generic-basis condition persists. The next datum is for this very cokernel by step 2, and $Q_n=0$ pulls back to zero. This proves (1) for every positive chain length.

A prescribed principal base restriction $B_0=D(a)$ containing $b$ is a special case of (1). Every resulting open in the affine schemes is principal: the inverse image of $D(a)$ is $D(f^\sharp(a))$. This follows from the inverse-image description of prime ideals under a spectrum map. Thus this base change is a standard shrinking. We may perform it first in all later constructions. Finitely many successive principal restrictions are still principal: in $R_a$, an open $D(h/a^m)$ corresponds to $D(ah)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. This also shows that principal restrictions constructed below over a smaller base are principal in the original schemes.

Fix a principal $W=D(g)\subset Y$ containing $y$. Its map to $B$ is smooth by open restriction, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, and hence open by the cited openness theorem. Choose a principal $B_1=D(a)$ containing $b$ inside its image. Set $Y_1=W\times_BB_1$ and $Z_1=\pi^{-1}(Y_1)$. Every fibre of $Y_1\to B_1$ is a nonempty open of the corresponding geometrically irreducible old fibre. It remains nonempty after every field extension, since field-extension maps on spectra are surjective and surjectivity survives base change. Such an open is irreducible: two nonempty opens in it are nonempty opens in the irreducible ambient fibre and hence intersect. Therefore the new fibres are geometrically irreducible. Open immersions are etale, so restriction retains smooth relative dimension $d$ by composition with relative dimension zero. By step 1, $Y\to B$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$; so each fibre $(Y_1)_c$, the spectrum of a finitely generated $\kappa(c)$-algebra because $Y_1$ is principal, is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], irreducible, with all local dimensions $d$, hence of dimension $d$ [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components]. Write $i^\sharp(h)=\pi^\sharp(g)$ for a lift $h\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, using surjectivity for the affine closed immersion. Put $X_1=D(hf^\sharp(a))$. Then $X_1$ lies over $B_1$ and $i^{-1}(X_1)=Z_1$. Consequently $i_1$ is the base change of $i$ and $\pi_1$ that of $\pi$; the sheaf identity restricts by step 2. All marked points remain, and the singleton fibre and purely transcendental extension are unchanged. This constructs the target shrinking in (2).

source.place: 05HA, lemma-shrink (2), with 056G (morphisms.tex, lemma-smooth-open) and the explicit lift used there

proof.text: For $U\subset X$ containing $x$, choose a principal $U_0\subset U$ containing $x$. The singleton-fibre neighbourhood lemma applied to $i^{-1}(U_0)\subset Z$ gives a neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ with $\pi^{-1}(V)\subset i^{-1}(U_0)$. Choose a principal $W$ with $y\in W\subset V$ and apply step 6. Its $Z_1$ lies in $i^{-1}(U_0)$; replace $X_1$ by $X_1\cap U_0$. This is principal (multiply the two defining functions), and its inverse image in $Z$ is still $Z_1$, so it changes none of the restricted sheaf identities or finite maps. It is contained in $U$, proving the initial-open request of (2).

For each restriction above, the pushforward really is the restriction of the old pushforward because $Z_1=\pi^{-1}(Y_1)$. On every open $T\subset Y_1$ both sheaves have sections $\mathcal G(\pi^{-1}T)$. Restrict $\alpha$ through this equality. Step 4's quotient computation gives its old cokernel restricted. The nonempty open $(Y_1)_b$ of $Y_b$ contains the same generic point: every nonempty open of an irreducible space contains its generic point, by the definition of generic point. Its local ring and residue field agree with the old ones because this is an open immersion; thus the residue-field map of $\alpha$ is the identical isomorphism. This proves the extra assertion about $\alpha$ in (2) and supplies the compatibility of all the restrictions used next.

source.place: 05HJ, lemma-base-change-complete, cokernel and generic-point argument applied to the restrictions of 05HA

proof.text: For the last-target request for a chain of length $n>0$, put $Y_0=X$. Start with the desired principal open $W\subset Y_n$. Apply step 6 to datum $n$, obtaining a principal restriction of its initial $Y_{n-1}$. Use that principal open as the target request for datum $n-1$. Continue backwards to datum 1. At each stage restrict the already treated later data only by the further principal base restriction, as allowed by step 5. After $n$ operations take the final base $B_*$. Every adjacent $Y_j$ now agrees from both sides: when treating datum $j$ its target was chosen to be exactly the previously selected initial open of datum $j+1$, further restricted to the current base. All opens are principal in the originals by step 5. By step 8 the cokernel passed from stage $j$ to $j+1$ is the same restricted cokernel; the generic-basis conditions and final zero remain. The last target is exactly $W\times_BB_*$, since subsequent operations changed it only by base restriction. This proves this request in (3).

For the initial-open request induct on the positive chain length. For length 1, steps 7--8 give the required chain restriction. For length $n>1$, first apply step 7 to datum 1, giving $B_1,X_1,Z_1,Y_1$ with $X_1\subset U$. Over $B_1$, the unchanged tail of length $n-1$ is a chain for $Q_1$ on the original $Y_1$ restricted to $B_1$ (step 5). By induction shrink that tail with its initial scheme a principal open $V$ contained in the head's chosen $Y_1$. First base-restrict the shrunk head to the base selected for the tail; then apply step 6 to that head with target request $V$ (viewed as principal in the head target by step 5). This gives a still smaller base $B_*$ and initial scheme contained in $X_1$, with head target exactly $V\times_{B_1}B_*$. Restrict the tail only along $B_*$. Step 8 identifies its initial module with the new head cokernel, so the pieces concatenate to a chain. Its initial scheme is contained in $U$. Together with steps 5 and 9 this proves all positive-length requests of (3), also after any prescribed principal base restriction.

source.place: 05HM, lemma-shrink-complete (3), induction and matching of the common target

proof.text: In length zero the initial sheaf is zero by definition. Base change keeps it zero. After any principal base restriction, choose a principal neighbourhood of the marked initial point inside the requested open and intersect it with the inverse image of the base restriction; the zero sheaf restricts to zero. No last target is requested. Finally every map occurring as an inclusion in a standard shrinking is an open immersion, and hence induces an isomorphism on the marked residue fields by the cited residue-field statement. This covers the zero-length case and the final residue-field assertion.
